source.text: 1. Μακρόθυμος, φησί, γίνου καὶ συνετός, καὶ πάντων τῶν πονηρῶν ἔργων κατακυριεύσεις καὶ ἐργάσῃ πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην. 2. ἐὰν γὰρ μακρόθυμος ἔσῃ, τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ κατοικοῦν ἐν σοὶ καθαρὸν ἔσται, μὴ ἐπισκοτούμενον ὑπὸ ἑτέρου πονηροῦ πνεύματος, ἀλλ' ἐν εὐρυχώρῳ κατοικοῦν ἀγαλλιάσεται καὶ εὐφρανθήσεται μετὰ τοῦ σκεύους ἐν ᾧ κατοικεῖ, καὶ λειτουργήσει τῷ Θεῷ ἐν ἱλαρότητι πολλῇ, ἔχον τὴν εὐθηνίαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ. 3. ἐὰν δὲ ὀξυχολία τις ἐπέλθῃ, εὐθὺς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, τρυφερὸν ὄν, στενοχωρεῖται, μὴ ἔχον [τὸν] τόπον καθαρόν, καὶ ζητεῖ ἀποστῆναι ἐκ τοῦ τόπου· πνίγεται γὰρ ὑπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ πνεύματος, μὴ ἔχον τόπον λειτουργῆσαι τῷ Κυρίῳ καθὼς βούλεται, μιαινόμενον ὑπὸ τῆς ὀξυχολίας. ἐν γὰρ τῇ μακροθυμίᾳ ὁ Κύριος κατοικεῖ, ἐν δὲ τῇ ὀξυχολίᾳ ὁ διάβολος. 4. ἀμφότερα οὖν τὰ πνεύματα ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ κατοικοῦντα, ἀσύμφορόν ἐστιν καὶ πονηρὸν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ ἐν ᾧ κατοικοῦσιν. 5. ἐὰν γὰρ λαβὼν ἀψίνθιον μικρὸν εἰς κεράμιον μέλιτος ἐπιχέῃς, οὐχὶ ὅλον τὸ μέλι ἀφανίζεται, καὶ τοσοῦτον μέλι ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐλαχίστου ἀψινθίου ἀπόλλυται καὶ ἀπόλλυσι τὴν γλυκύτητα τοῦ μέλιτος, καὶ οὐκέτι τὴν αὐτὴν χάριν ἔχει παρὰ τῷ δεσπότῃ, ὅτι ἐπικράνθη καὶ τὴν χρῆσιν αὐτοῦ ἀπώλεσεν; ἐὰν δὲ εἰς τὸ μέλι μὴ βληθῇ τὸ ἀψίνθιον, γλυκὺ εὑρίσκεται τὸ μέλι καὶ εὔχρηστον γίνεται τῷ δεσπότῃ αὐτοῦ. 6. βλέπεις [οὖν] ὅτι ἡ μακροθυμία γλυκυτάτη ἐστὶν ὑπὲρ τὸ μέλι καὶ εὔχρηστός ἐστι τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ κατοικεῖ. ἡ δὲ ὀξυχολία πικρὰ καὶ ἄχρηστός ἐστιν. ἐὰν οὖν μιγῇ ἡ ὀξυχολία τῇ μακροθυμίᾳ, μιαίνεται ἡ μακροθυμία, καὶ οὐκ εὔχρηστός ἐστι τῷ Θε ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ, μηδὲν ἐν ἑαυτῇ ἔχουσα πικρόν, παραμένουσα διὰ παντὸς πραεῖα καὶ ἡσύχιος. αὕτη οὖν ἡ μακροθυμία κατοικεῖ μετὰ τῶν τὴν πίστιν ἐχόντων ὁλόκληρον. 4. ἡ δὲ ὀξυχολία πρῶτον μὲν μωρά ἐστιν, ἐλαφρά τε καὶ ἄφρων. εἶτα ἐκ τῆς ἀφροσύνης γίνεται πικρία, ἐκ δὲ τῆς πικρίας θυμός, ἐκ δὲ τοῦ θυμοῦ ὀργή, ἐκ δὲ τῆς ὀργῆς μῆνις· εἶτα ἡ μῆνις ἐκ τοσούτων κακῶν συνισταμένη γίνεται ἁμαρτία μεγάλη καὶ ἀνίατος. 5. ὅταν γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ πνεύματα πάντα ἐν ἑνὶ ἀγγείῳ κατοικῇ, οὗ καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατοικεῖ, οὐ χωρεῖ τὸ ἄγγος ἐκεῖνο, ἀλλ' ὑπερπλεονάζει. 6. τὸ τρυφερὸν οὖν πνεῦμα, μὴ ἔχον συνήθειαν μετὰ πονηροῦ πνεύματος κατοικεῖν μηδὲ μετὰ σκληρότητος, ἀποχωρεῖ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοῦ τοιούτου καὶ ζητεῖ κατοικεῖν μετὰ πραότητος καὶ ἡσυχίας. 7. εἶτα ὅταν ἀποστῇ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου οὗ κατοικεῖ, γίνεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος κενὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ δικαίου, καὶ τὸ λοιπὸν πεπληρωμένος τοῖς πνεύμασι τοῖς πονηροῖς ἀκαταστατεῖ ἐν πάσῃ πράξει αὐτοῦ, περισπώμενος ὧδε κἀκεῖ ἀπὸ τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν πονηρῶν, καὶ ὅλως ἀποτυφλοῦται ἀπὸ τῆς διανοίας τῆς ἀγαθῆς. οὕτως οὖν συμβαίνει πᾶσι τοῖς ὀξυχόλοις. 8. ἀπέχου οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς ὀξυχολίας, τοῦ πονηροτάτου πνεύματος· ἔνδυσαι δὲ τὴν μακροθυμίαν καὶ ἀντίστα τῇ ὀξυχολίᾳ καὶ τῇ πικρίᾳ, καὶ ἔσῃ εὑρισκόμενος μετὰ τῆς σεμνότητος τῆς ἠγαπημένης ὑπὸ τοῦ Κυρίου. βλέπε οὖν μήποτε παρενθυμηθῇς τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην· ἐὰν γὰρ ταύτης τῆς ἐντολῆς κυριεύσῃς, καὶ τὰς λοιπὰς ἐντολὰς δυνήσῃ φυλάξαι, ἅς σοι μέλλω ἐντέλλεσθαι. ἰσχυροῦ ἐν αὐταῖς καὶ ἐνδυναμοῦ, καὶ πάντες ἐνδυναμούσθωσαν ὅσοι ἐὰν θέλωσιν ἐν αὐταῖς πορεύεσθαι.

translation.text:
“Be long-suffering[1],” he says, “and sensible, and you will gain mastery over all wicked deeds and do every work of righteousness. For if you are long-suffering, the holy spirit[2] that dwells in you will be pure, not being clouded by another evil spirit; rather, dwelling in a wide space[3] it will exult and rejoice with the vessel in which it dwells, and it will minister[4] to God with much cheerfulness, having vitality[5] within itself.

But if a quick temper[6] comes on, at once the holy spirit—being tender—is cramped, not having a clean place, and it seeks to withdraw from that place; for it is choked by the evil spirit, not having room to minister to the Lord as it desires, being defiled by the quick temper. For in long-suffering the Lord dwells, but in quick temper, the devil. Therefore when both spirits dwell together in one, it is unprofitable and harmful to that person in whom they dwell.

For if, after taking a little wormwood[7], you pour it into a jar of honey, does not all the honey perish? So much honey is ruined by the smallest amount of wormwood: it destroys the sweetness of the honey, and it no longer has the same favor with its master[8], because it has been embittered and has lost its use. But if the wormwood is not cast into the honey, the honey is found sweet and becomes serviceable to its master.

You see, then, that long-suffering is sweeter than honey and is serviceable to the Lord, and he dwells in it; but quick temper is bitter and useless. If, therefore, quick temper is mixed with long-suffering, long-suffering is defiled and is no longer useful to God. Long-suffering at all times has nothing bitter within itself, remaining always gentle and quiet. This long-suffering, then, dwells with those who have the faith complete[10].

Quick temper, for its part, is first foolish—flighty and senseless. Then from senselessness comes bitterness; from bitterness, anger; from anger, wrath; and from wrath, rage. Then rage—composed of so many evils—becomes a great and incurable sin.

For when all these spirits dwell in one vessel, the very vessel in which the holy spirit also dwells, that vessel cannot contain them; it overflows. The tender spirit, having no habit of dwelling with an evil spirit or with hardness, withdraws from such a person and seeks to dwell with gentleness and quiet. Then, when it has departed from that person in whom it dwells, that person becomes empty of the righteous spirit[11]; and thereafter, being filled with evil spirits, he is unstable in all his deeds, dragged here and there by the evil spirits, and is altogether blinded as to his good understanding. Thus it happens to all who are quick-tempered.

Therefore keep away from quick temper—that most wicked spirit—but clothe yourself with long-suffering, and stand against quick temper and bitterness, and you will be found with the dignity[9] that is beloved by the Lord. See to it, then, that you never forget[12] this command; for if you gain mastery of this command, you will also be able to keep the other commands that I am about to give you. Be strong in them and be empowered, and let all be empowered who wish to walk in them.”

ἐὰν δὲ εἰς τὸ μέλι μὴ βληθῇ τὸ ἀψίνθιον, γλυκὺ εὑρίσκεται τὸ μέλι καὶ εὔχρηστον γίνεται τῷ δεσπότῃ αὐτοῦ. 6. βλέπεις [οὖν] ὅτι ἡ μακροθυμία γλυκυτάτη ἐστὶν ὑπὲρ τὸ μέλι καὶ εὔχρηστός ἐστι τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ κατοικεῖ. ἡ δὲ ὀξυχολία πικρὰ καὶ ἄχρηστός ἐστιν. ἐὰν οὖν μιγῇ ἡ ὀξυχολία τῇ μακροθυμίᾳ, μιαίνεται ἡ μακροθυμία, καὶ οὐκ εὔχρηστός ἐστι τῷ Θε ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ, μηδὲν ἐν ἑαυτῇ ἔχουσα πικρόν, παραμένουσα διὰ παντὸς πραεῖα καὶ ἡσύχιος. αὕτη οὖν ἡ μακροθυμία κατοικεῖ μετὰ τῶν τὴν πίστιν ἐχόντων ὁλόκληρον. 4. ἡ δὲ ὀξυχολία πρῶτον μὲν μωρά ἐστιν, ἐλαφρά τε καὶ ἄφρων. εἶτα ἐκ τῆς ἀφροσύνης γίνεται πικρία, ἐκ δὲ τῆς πικρίας θυμός, ἐκ δὲ τοῦ θυμοῦ ὀργή, ἐκ δὲ τῆς ὀργῆς μῆνις· εἶτα ἡ μῆνις ἐκ τοσούτων κακῶν συνισταμένη γίνεται ἁμαρτία μεγάλη καὶ ἀνίατος. 5. ὅταν γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ πνεύματα πάντα ἐν ἑνὶ ἀγγείῳ κατοικῇ, οὗ καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατοικεῖ, οὐ χωρεῖ τὸ ἄγγος ἐκεῖνο, ἀλλ' ὑπερπλεονάζει. 6. τὸ τρυφερὸν οὖν πνεῦμα, μὴ ἔχον συνήθειαν μετὰ πονηροῦ πνεύματος κατοικεῖν μηδὲ μετὰ σκληρότητος, ἀποχωρεῖ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοῦ τοιούτου καὶ ζητεῖ κατοικεῖν μετὰ πραότητος καὶ ἡσυχίας. 7. εἶτα ὅταν ἀποστῇ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου οὗ κατοικεῖ, γίνεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος κενὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ δικαίου, καὶ τὸ λοιπὸν πεπληρωμένος τοῖς πνεύμασι τοῖς πονηροῖς ἀκαταστατεῖ ἐν πάσῃ πράξει αὐτοῦ, περισπώμενος ὧδε κἀκεῖ ἀπὸ τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν πονηρῶν, καὶ ὅλως ἀποτυφλοῦται ἀπὸ τῆς διανοίας τῆς ἀγαθῆς. οὕτως οὖν συμβαίνει πᾶσι τοῖς ὀξυχόλοις. 8. ἀπέχου οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς ὀξυχολίας, τοῦ πονηροτάτου πνεύματος· ἔνδυσαι δὲ τὴν μακροθυμίαν καὶ ἀντίστα τῇ ὀξυχολίᾳ καὶ τῇ πικρίᾳ, καὶ ἔσῃ εὑρισκόμενος μετὰ τῆς σεμνότητος τῆς ἠγαπημένης ὑπὸ τοῦ Κυρίου. βλέπε οὖν μήποτε παρενθυμηθῇς τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην· ἐὰν γὰρ ταύτης τῆς ἐντολῆς κυριεύσῃς, καὶ τὰς λοιπὰς ἐντολὰς δυνήσῃ φυλάξαι, ἅς σοι μέλλω ἐντέλλεσθαι. ἰσχυροῦ ἐν αὐταῖς καὶ ἐνδυναμοῦ, καὶ πάντες ἐνδυναμούσθωσαν ὅσοι ἐὰν θέλωσιν ἐν αὐταῖς πορεύεσθαι.

translation.text: But if a quick temper comes on, at once the holy spirit—being tender—is cramped, not having a clean place, and it seeks to withdraw from that place; for it is choked by the evil spirit, not having room to minister to the Lord as it desires, being defiled by the quick temper. For in long-suffering the Lord dwells, but in quick temper the devil. Therefore, when both spirits dwell together in one, it is unprofitable and harmful to that person in whom they dwell.

translation.text: For if, after taking a little wormwood, you pour it into a jar of honey, does not all the honey perish? So much honey is ruined by the smallest amount of wormwood: it destroys the sweetness of the honey, and it no longer has the same usefulness with its master, because it has been embittered and has lost its use. But if the wormwood is not cast into the honey, the honey is found sweet and becomes serviceable to its master.

translation.text: You see, then, that long-suffering is sweeter than honey and is serviceable to the Lord, and he dwells in it; but quick temper is bitter and useless. If, therefore, quick temper is mixed with long-suffering, long-suffering is defiled and is no longer useful to God. Long-suffering at all times has nothing bitter within itself, remaining always gentle and quiet. This long-suffering, then, dwells with those who have the faith complete.

translation.text: For when all these spirits dwell in one vessel, the very vessel in which the holy spirit also dwells, that vessel cannot contain them; it overflows. The tender spirit, having no habit of dwelling with an evil spirit or with harshness, withdraws from such a person and seeks to dwell with gentleness and quiet. Then, when it has departed from that person in whom it dwells, that person becomes empty of the righteous spirit; and thereafter, being filled with evil spirits, he is unstable in all his deeds, dragged here and there by the evil spirits, and is altogether blinded from his good understanding. Thus it happens to all who are quick-tempered.

translation.text: Therefore keep away from quick temper—that most wicked spirit—but clothe yourself with long-suffering, and stand against quick temper and bitterness, and you will be found with the dignity that is beloved by the Lord. See to it, then, that you never neglect this command; for if you gain mastery over this command, you will also be able to keep the other commands that I am about to give you. Be strong in them and be empowered[—], and let all be empowered who wish to walk in them.”

base_translation.text: “Be long-suffering,” he says, “and sensible, and you will gain mastery over all wicked deeds and do every work of righteousness. For if you are long-suffering, the holy spirit that dwells in you will be pure, not being darkened by another evil spirit; rather, dwelling in a wide space it will exult and rejoice with the vessel in which it dwells, and it will minister to God with much cheerfulness, having prosperity within itself.

translation.text: “Be patient,” he says, “and use good judgment. Then you will overcome every wicked deed and do every righteous work. For if you are patient, the holy spirit living in you will be pure and will not be darkened by another evil spirit. Instead, it will live in a spacious place. It will celebrate and rejoice with the person in whom it lives, and it will serve God very gladly, enjoying well-being within itself.”

spob_revision_history.previous_text: “Be patient,” he says, “and use good judgment. Then you will overcome every wicked deed and do everything that is right. If you are patient, the holy spirit living in you will remain pure and will not be darkened by another evil spirit. Instead, it will live with room to flourish. It will celebrate and rejoice together with the body where it lives, and it will serve God very gladly, enjoying peace and well-being within.”
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft successfully makes long-suffering, sensibility, and the Spirit’s glad service accessible. Revision is needed because it broadens “every work of righteousness,” specifies the vessel as a physical body despite a live broader-person ambiguity, and adds “peace” to the Spirit’s inward prosperity. The recommended wording preserves the source’s distinct moral category, its dwelling imagery, and its broad positive inner condition while remaining clear.

base_translation.text: For if, after taking a little wormwood, you pour it into a jar of honey, does not all the honey perish? So much honey is ruined by the smallest amount of wormwood: it destroys the sweetness of the honey, and it no longer has the same usefulness with its master, because it has been embittered and has lost its use. But if the wormwood is not cast into the honey, the honey is found sweet and becomes serviceable to its master.

Long-suffering at all times has nothing bitter within itself, remaining always gentle and quiet. This long-suffering, then, dwells with those who have the faith complete.

base_translation.text: Quick temper, for its part, is first foolish—flighty and senseless. Then from senselessness comes bitterness; from bitterness, anger; from anger, wrath; and from wrath, rage. Then rage—composed of so many evils—becomes a great and incurable sin.

translation.text: A quick temper begins as foolishness—reckless and without good sense. This lack of sense leads to bitterness; bitterness leads to anger; anger leads to wrath; and wrath leads to rage. Rage, built from so many evils, then becomes a great sin that cannot be cured.

risk_flags.risk: “Cannot be cured” may be mistaken for a general doctrine that such sin cannot be forgiven.
risk_flags.mitigation: The wording retains the passage’s moral-medical image without adding a claim about forgiveness.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: A quick temper begins as foolishness—reckless and without good sense. This lack of sense leads to bitterness; bitterness leads to anger; anger leads to wrath; and wrath leads to rage. Rage, built from all these evils, then becomes a great sin that is very hard to cure.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft clearly communicates the escalating sequence and appropriately explains “flighty and senseless” in common language. However, its final wording softens “incurable” to “very hard to cure,” which is not warranted by the POB wording. Retain the absolute image, while recognizing that the passage itself uses a moral/medical metaphor and does not here define a doctrine of forgiveness.

base_translation.text: For when all these spirits dwell in one vessel, the very vessel in which the holy spirit also dwells, that vessel cannot contain them; it overflows. The tender spirit, having no habit of dwelling with an evil spirit or with harshness, withdraws from such a person and seeks to dwell with gentleness and quiet. Then, when it has departed from that person in whom it dwells, that person becomes empty of the righteous spirit; and thereafter, being filled with evil spirits, he is unstable in all his deeds, dragged here and there by the evil spirits, and is altogether blinded from his good understanding. Thus it happens to all who are quick-tempered.

translation.text: When all these spirits live in the same vessel as the holy spirit, that vessel cannot hold them all and overflows. The tender spirit is not accustomed to living with an evil spirit or with harshness, so it leaves that person and seeks a home where there is gentleness and peace. Once the righteous spirit has left, the person is empty of it and becomes filled with evil spirits. Those spirits pull him this way and that, making him unstable in everything he does and completely unable to understand what is good. This is what happens to everyone who is quick-tempered.

base_translation.text: Therefore keep away from quick temper—that most wicked spirit—but clothe yourself with long-suffering, and stand against quick temper and bitterness, and you will be found with the dignity that is beloved by the Lord. See to it, then, that you never neglect this command; for if you gain mastery over this command, you will also be able to keep the other commands that I am about to give you.
